prompt: One module's row in the export table reads 5 exported functions, 1 exported list or constant, and 1 export that reads a date against today. Which module is it?
options: complianceStatus
documentControl
calendar
auditManagement
explanation: The calendar sits under all five apps. complianceStatus reads 11, 8 and 4, documentControl 14, 7 and 4, and auditManagement 4 that read a date.

prompt: Of these four inputs, which one does parseDateOnly read as a real day?
options: 2027-02-28, which daysUntil counts as 136.
2026-13-01, as the next year's first day.
2026-02-30, rolled into March.
tbc, read as the as-of date until a date is confirmed.
explanation: 2026-13-01 names a thirteenth month and 2026-02-30 a day February does not have, so both print null. tbc is no date. The calendar refuses instead of guessing.

prompt: When the date passed as today cannot be read, the register refuses while the library answers Review scheduled for a published document whose review date is 2020-01-06. Why the two behaviours?
options: The library reads its own clock instead.
Review scheduled is the library's refusal.
Old review dates are exempt from the check.
Only deriveStatus refuses an unreadable today, which is AS15 Q1.
explanation: The register's refusal is the RangeError deriveStatus throws. The library's Review scheduled is an answer given as though nothing were due, a held limit of the digest, and it says nothing about the document.

prompt: Remove the expiry from REG-2026-005, the radioactive source licence, and change nothing else. What does it read?
options: Expired, as before the field was removed.
On track, counted to its due date of 2026-12-31.
No date set, because a licence with no expiry has no date to count.
Overdue, counted to the old expiry.
explanation: With the expiry removed the due date of 2026-12-31 is the next action date. It is ahead and outside the window, so the licence reads On track, the same as with the expiry moved to 2027-09-30.

prompt: In complianceStatus.STATUS_SEVERITY, which status sits immediately below Draft?
options: Not applicable
No date set
Superseded
Compliant
explanation: The list runs Expired, Overdue, Due soon, On track, Compliant, No date set, Draft, Superseded and Not applicable. Draft is seventh and Superseded eighth.

prompt: REG-2026-011, the night noise permit, has a due date of 2026-05-01 that has passed, and its lifecycle reads Not applicable. What status does the register show?
options: Not applicable
Overdue
Expired
No date set
explanation: For Draft, Superseded and Not applicable the lifecycle is the status. The permit does not bind this operator, so its passed date prints a day count and drives no warning.

prompt: REG-2026-010, the safety case resubmission, has a due date of 2027-06-30 and reads Draft. What does the Draft lifecycle mean for the row?
options: It is due in 258 days and will turn On track.
It has been replaced by another obligation.
It does not bind the operator.
It is still being set up, so nobody is warned about it.
explanation: A Draft is a record not yet in force, so warning anyone about it would be wrong. An obligation replaced by another is Superseded; one that does not bind the operator is Not applicable.

prompt: REG-2026-012 and REG-2026-001 are both Due soon. Which sorts first in byUrgency, and why?
options: REG-2026-001, an expiry outranks a due date.
REG-2026-001, because a lead time set on the record outranks the default.
REG-2026-012, Financial sorts above Environmental.
explanation: Both carry the same status, so byUrgency sorts them by the nearest next action date: 2026-11-09 for the rental and 2026-11-20 for the permit. They sit fourth and fifth.

prompt: REG-2026-003 is due 16 days after the as-of date. Of these lead times, which leaves it On track?
options: null
explanation: The table prints 0, 7, 14 and 15 as On track. 17 and 90 reach the 16 days that remain, and null is replaced by the default window, so all three read Due soon.

prompt: The flare return's lead time field holds an empty string. What does the return read?
options: Due soon, the same as with no lead time set at all.
On track, an empty field opens no window.
On track, as with its recorded 14.
Overdue, an empty field reads as zero.
explanation: An empty string is not a usable lead time, so the engine applies DEFAULT_LEAD_TIME_DAYS. The digest prints '' (empty) as Due soon, beside null, -5, 'ten' and a field left out.

prompt: An Annual and a Biennial obligation both fall due 2026-10-31. On which dates do their current periods begin?
options: 2026-04-30 and 2025-10-31, a half year and a year back.
2026-07-31 and 2026-04-30, a quarter and a half year back.
2026-09-30 and 2025-10-31, a month and a year back.
explanation: periodStart steps one frequency back from the next due date. October has a thirty-first, so neither start is pulled back: Annual reads 2025-10-31 at -349 days and Biennial 2024-10-31 at -714.

prompt: summarise prints in review 1 for the IKORO library. Which document is it?
options: HSE-PRO-0012, the draft.
ENG-PRO-0019, the hydrotest procedure.
OPS-PLA-0002, the terminal emergency response plan.
OPS-PHI-0001, the philosophy.
explanation: ENG-PRO-0019 is the one document with the status In Review, and its revision rev-0019-10 carries the reviewer rule. HSE-PRO-0012 is a Draft, and OPS-PLA-0002 is Published and reads Review due soon.

prompt: After the late filing of REG-2026-002 is recorded, rollForward moves its due date from 2026-10-10 to 2026-11-10. Why does the filing on 2026-10-14 count for the new period?
options: The filing is within a month of the old due date, and any filing in that month counts.
Its periodStart is 2026-10-14, the filing date.
The rolled row's periodStart is 2026-10-10, and the filing is on or after it.
Any filing recorded after a due date is carried into the period that follows it.
explanation: This joins the current period rule and the roll. Stepping one month back from 2026-11-10 gives 2026-10-10, so a filing dated 2026-10-14 falls inside the period and counts.

prompt: A quarterly obligation last due on 2026-08-31 is rolled on. Where does it land, and how many days from the as-of date?
explanation: November has thirty days, so the date is pulled back to 2026-11-30, which daysUntil counts as 46. 2027-02-28 at 136 is the Semi-annual roll.

prompt: The date 2026-09-30 appears in both the rollForward table and the periodStart table. Which two calls produce it?
options: The Quarterly roll from 2026-08-31, and the Quarterly period start for 2026-10-31.
The Monthly roll from 2026-08-31, and the Semi-annual period start for 2026-10-31.
The Semi-annual roll from 2026-08-31, and the Monthly period start for 2026-10-31.
The Monthly roll from 2026-08-31, and the Monthly period start for 2026-10-31.
explanation: rollForward steps forward from a due date and periodStart steps back from one, and both pull a thirty-first back when the month is shorter. The Semi-annual roll from 2026-03-31 lands there too.

prompt: Which app holds audits, checklists, findings and audit programmes, and which engine module backs it?
options: ISO Compliance, backed by isoCompliance.
The Audit & Findings Manager, backed by auditManagement.
Quality Assurance Plan & NCR, backed by qualityAssurance.
Document Control, backed by documentControl.
explanation: Each of the five apps is backed by one module, with the calendar under all of them. ISO Compliance holds a clause register for a standard, and the Quality Assurance Plan & NCR app holds inspection and test plans and NCRs.

prompt: Which next due date, and which day count, does the digest print for the Biennial roll from 2026-08-31?
explanation: Biennial steps two years and August keeps its thirty-first. 2027-08-31 at 320 days is the Annual roll.

prompt: The month end rule works in three places across these apps. A document issued on 2024-02-29 on a 12 month review period comes up for review when?
options: 2025-02-28, pulled back the same way rollForward pulls a due date back.
2026-02-28, pushed a further year on because February 2025 has no twenty-ninth.
2024-02-29, the issue date, because a leap day cannot be rolled.
No date, because nextReviewDate refuses to count from a leap day.
explanation: nextReviewDate prints 2025-02-28 at -594 days. rollForward does the same to 2028-02-29 rolled Annual, giving 2029-02-28, so a due date, its period and a review date agree about month ends.

prompt: A semi-annual schedule is rolled from 2026-08-31 to 2027-02-28. Where does the following semi-annual roll land?
explanation: The digest prints 2026-08-31, 2027-02-28 and then 2027-08-28 for Semi-annual. The second step starts from the twenty-eighth it landed on in February. 2027-08-31 is the Annual roll from 2026-08-31, 2028-08-31 the Biennial one, and 2027-02-28 is the first step itself.

prompt: A department 'Operations' files a 'Plan'. Which document number prefix comes back?
options: OPS-PLA
OPE-PLA
OP-PL
GEN-DOC
explanation: documentPrefix takes the first three letters of each. OPS-PLA-0002 is a number as it stands in the library, and the digest does not say how it was issued. GEN-DOC is what an empty department and category give.

prompt: atLeastConfidential is read against the default floor Confidential. What does it answer for Internal and for Restricted?
options: true for both, because each is a restricted class.
true for Internal only.
false for Internal and true for Restricted.
false for both, because only Confidential meets the floor.
explanation: atLeastConfidential answers true at the floor or above it. The digest prints Public false, Internal false, Confidential true and Restricted true.

prompt: Two issue dates, each with its own review period, are sent by nextReviewDate to the same review date of 2026-02-28. Which two?
options: 2024-08-31 on 18 months, and 2025-12-31 on 2 months.
2024-08-31 on 18 months, and 2024-02-29 on 12 months.
2025-12-31 on 2 months, and 2025-11-02 on 12 months.
2024-02-29 on 12 months, and 2025-06-30 on 24 months.
explanation: Both land on the last day of February, which has no thirty-first, at -229 days. 2024-02-29 on 12 months gives 2025-02-28, and 2025-11-02 on 12 months gives 2026-11-02.

prompt: A review period of 0 months is passed with the issue date 2025-03-14. What comes back from nextReviewDate?
options: 2025-03-14, the issue date itself
2027-03-14, from the default
A refusal naming the period
none
explanation: A period of 0 returns none, and so does a period of null. 2027-03-14 appears only when the caller passes DEFAULT_REVIEW_PERIOD_MONTHS, and the default is the caller's to apply.

prompt: A review task on rev-0019-10 has already been approved, and somebody decides it again. What does the engine answer?
options: ALLOWED, as a second approval.
REFUSED: This review task is already approved.
REFUSED: Only the reviewer this task is assigned to can decide it.
ALLOWED, provided the decision is made by the assigned reviewer.
explanation: An approval on the record stays the approval that was given, so a second decision on the same task is refused.

prompt: Which two of the seven requests on rev-0019-10 does the engine allow?
options: An independent reviewer is assigned; somebody else decides it for the reviewer.
The author assigns herself; the assigned reviewer decides a pending task.
An independent reviewer is assigned; the assigned reviewer decides a pending task.
No reviewer is chosen; the assigned reviewer decides a pending task.
explanation: Both allowed requests have two named people on the record who are different. The author assigning herself, no reviewer, a stand-in decider, the author deciding and a second decision are refused.

prompt: nextRevisionNumber is given ' 04 ', with spaces around it. What does it return?
explanation: The spaces are ignored and the number inside is read, and the width of two digits is kept. '01' is what a revision that is not a number gives.

prompt: summarise over the 7 IKORO documents counts Obsolete 0 and Rejected 0. What does printing those zeros tell the reader?
options: The two statuses are switched off in this library.
The engine could not read those statuses, so it printed a placeholder.
Obsolete and Rejected documents are kept in a separate archive that summarise does not see.
They were counted, and none were found.
explanation: A zero printed beside a status is a finding in its own right. The library's counts read Draft 1, In Review 1, Approved 1, Published 3, Superseded 1, Obsolete 0 and Rejected 0.

prompt: A caller passes DEFAULT_REVIEW_PERIOD_MONTHS for a document issued 2025-03-14. What review date comes back?
options: none
explanation: DEFAULT_REVIEW_PERIOD_MONTHS is 24, and 24 months on from 2025-03-14 is 2027-03-14, 150 days from the as-of date. 2028-10-01 is what counting from a correction would give.

prompt: HSE-PRO-0007 was issued 2024-09-30 on a 24 month period. Its recorded next review is 2026-09-30. What does the digest's recomputation show?
options: The recomputed date disagrees and the record has to be corrected.
Nothing, an overdue document is left out.
The recomputed date agrees with the one on record: true.
The recomputed date agrees only once the default period is applied.
explanation: nextReviewDate from 2024-09-30 on 24 months gives 2026-09-30, and the digest prints true for the two agreeing. OPS-PLA-0002 and ENG-STD-0011 agree as well.

prompt: Why can nextReviewDate give OPS-PHI-0001, the flare management philosophy, no review date?
options: Its review period is 0.
It is not in force.
Philosophies are exempt from review.
It has no issue date on the record to count from.
explanation: The digest names four documents with no issue date recorded: OPS-PHI-0001, OPS-PRO-0004, HSE-PRO-0012 and ENG-PRO-0019. OPS-PHI-0001 is Published and in force, and reads No review scheduled.

prompt: byUrgency sorts the register and byReviewUrgency sorts the library. Which rule do the two sorts share?
options: The state comes first, then the nearest date, and undated records go last.
The nearest date comes first, whatever the state, and undated records go first.
The code or document number decides, and the state only breaks ties.
The oldest record comes first, because it has waited longest for attention.
explanation: In both, the states that need action lead the list and records that are not live go to the bottom. A reader who has learned one sort can read the other.

prompt: An obligation can carry its own lead time. What sets the width of the Review due soon window for a controlled document?
options: Each document's own lead time, or the default.
One constant for the module, documentControl.REVIEW_LEAD_DAYS.
The review period in months, read as days.
DEFAULT_REVIEW_PERIOD_MONTHS, in days.
explanation: The register reads each obligation's lead time and falls back on DEFAULT_LEAD_TIME_DAYS. The library's window is REVIEW_LEAD_DAYS, and OPS-PLA-0002 at 18 days reads Review due soon.

prompt: REG-2026-013 carries the frequency Other and has no dates. What do rollForward and the register give it?
options: The date one year on, and On track.
A refusal, and Draft until a date is entered.
No next date, and Overdue since nothing was filed.
No next date from rollForward, and No date set on the register.
explanation: Other names no interval, so rollForward gives none. With no due date and no expiry the status is No date set, and somebody who knows the date has to enter it.

prompt: Two Compliant reasons are "Last filed 2026-08-05, next due in" a number of days, and "Filed 2026-08-10. A one-off obligation, nothing further is due." Which obligations give them?
options: REG-2026-006 gives the first and REG-2026-008 the second.
REG-2026-003 gives the first and REG-2026-006 the second.
REG-2026-008 gives the first and REG-2026-006 the second.
REG-2026-008 gives the first and REG-2026-007 the second.
explanation: The community report has a filing inside its current period and a next due date. The right of way consent is a filed One-off, which rollForward cannot move on, so nothing further is due.

prompt: Two regimes hold a single IKORO obligation each, Financial and Licensing. Name the obligation in each.
options: The concession rental is Financial; the radioactive source licence is Licensing.
The radioactive source licence is Financial; the concession rental is Licensing.
The concession rental is Financial; the right of way consent is Licensing.
The discharge permit is Financial; the radioactive source licence is Licensing.
explanation: REG-2026-012, the concession rental, is Financial, a Fee or levy. REG-2026-005, the radioactive source licence, is Licensing, a Licence. The right of way consent is Operational and the discharge permit is Environmental.

prompt: What obligation type does the regime table give REG-2026-007, the oil spill contingency plan notification?
options: Consent
Periodic report
Permit
Notification
explanation: REG-2026-007 is Health & Safety by regime and Notification by type. Consent is the right of way consent's type.

prompt: Why does every status and day count in this tier carry the as-of date 2026-10-15 beside it?
options: It is the date the IKORO records were last edited by hand.
Each is derived against that date and is true at no other.
It is the date the regulator fixed for every return in the register.
It is the date the machine clock read when the digest was built, which the engine records.
explanation: Move the as-of date and the same record reads differently with nobody having edited it. The digest never read the machine clock.

prompt: The monthly water quality return is filed late and rolled on. Of the summarise counts, which one loses it?
options: Due soon
Compliant
Overdue
Expired
explanation: As recorded it reads Overdue. After the filing and the roll the digest prints status Due soon, so it leaves Overdue and joins Due soon, which is still an attention status.

prompt: REG-2026-003 is given a lead time of 16 in place of its recorded 14. Which summarise count loses it?
options: On track
Due soon
Compliant
Overdue
explanation: With 14 it reads On track and with 16 it reads Due soon, so it leaves On track and joins Due soon, one of the attention statuses.

prompt: HSE-PRO-0012, the oily waste handling procedure, is a Draft with no review date. Where does it sit in the review queue?
options: Fourth, as No review scheduled, above every document not in force.
First, because a Draft with no review date is the most urgent gap.
Seventh, below the hydrotest procedure that is In Review.
Sixth: Not in force and undated.
explanation: Draft is outside EFFECTIVE_STATUSES, so its state is Not in force. Among the three not in force, OPS-PRO-0004 comes first because it has a review date, then HSE-PRO-0012 and ENG-PRO-0019.

prompt: The next tier's checklists record an answer for each item. Which list is auditManagement.ANSWERED_RESULTS?
options: Passed, Failed, Waived and Not applicable
Conformant, Nonconformant, Observation and Not applicable
Critical, Major, Minor, Observation
Hold point, Witness point, Review point
explanation: Critical, Major, Minor and Observation are the NCR severities. The Hold, Witness and Review points are three of the five point types.

prompt: REG-2026-002's reason reads "The due date passed 5 days ago." What days until does the register print beside it?
explanation: A passed date is a negative count, and the reason says it in words. -15 is the expired licence and -14 is the licence varied to a due date of 2026-10-01.
